A signed-in alarm may have one shared definition and a separate
      “Rings On” choice for each eligible device. A local-only
      alarm can ring only on the installation where it was created. A target
      choice is a request, not proof that a device scheduled or canceled the

A signed-in user can delete one connected XTimers account. This removes
      that account's data from the XTimers service, including active timers,
      alarms, session and task history, device-targeting and scheduling-status
      records, snapshots, sounds, Background Library content, feedback,
      reminders, messages, published reports and report links, SMS configuration,
      and push-registration data. XTimers makes a
      best-effort attempt to cancel alarms scheduled by that installation before
      removing its local account state.
      The Xin Account, shared sign-in identity, and any other connected product
      accounts remain available.

Acceptable Use
Account and service availability apply. SMS and calls need your own eligible, verified number and separate consent. Calls support USA/Canada numbers, use English and do not automatically redial.

Active shared alarm definitions, current device targets, and current
      delivery status are retained while needed to provide the connected
      XTimers account. Records that an alarm was deleted and evidence that it
      was canceled are kept for at least 90 days, and longer when an active
      device target has not confirmed cancellation. This prevents an offline
      device from incorrectly recreating or continuing the alarm. Retired or
      stale devices may keep their last truthful reported status. This
      operational retention does not replace an authenticated request to
      delete the XTimers account itself.

Automatic Activity Tracking
Automatic app activity tracking images

Automatic application tracking can be enabled or disabled in XTimers
      settings. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available
      only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition, where browser
      integration can also be enabled or disabled. Activity records, including
      raw stored web addresses and titles, stay on the Mac. While tracking runs,
      raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops
      XTimers app recording and integration but keeps existing history; use
      Reset tracked data to erase it. Disable or remove the separately installed
      browser extension to stop its own active-tab queries and local delivery
      attempts.
      If the user explicitly emails or publishes a report, it can include the displayed
      application names and derived website hostnames, but not those raw web
      addresses or titles.

On iPhone and iPad, AlarmKit authorization and system scheduling are
      handled by Apple. On Mac, alarms require the Mac to be awake, XTimers to
      be running, and required permissions. Stop, snooze, fire, and cancellation
      actions can be synchronized so other installations can update their
      status, but an offline installation may act later or continue ringing.

On iPhone and iPad, system alarm delivery depends on AlarmKit
      authorization and operating-system scheduling. On Mac, delivery requires
      the Mac to be awake, XTimers to be running, and required permissions to
      remain available. Offline devices can act later and may continue ringing
      until they receive and apply an update. Stop or snooze actions can take
      time to appear on another device. Do not treat XTimers as a guaranteed
      delivery service.

Sign in with Apple, Google, an email code or a password. Some device settings and local-only data remain on their own device.

Signing out ends XTimers access on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation before hiding its signed-in alarm state;
      a pending or failed cancellation remains truthful when confirmation is
      unavailable. Signing out preserves local timers and other local data;
      XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset
      on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Removing or uninstalling the app can leave
      Application Support, container, or backup copies, depending on the
      platform and system settings. Signing out or uninstalling does not delete
      the Xin Account or server copies of connected XTimers data; use the
      authenticated account-deletion actions for that purpose.

Signing out ends XTimers sign-in on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. It does not delete the Xin Account, XTimers server data,
      or local timers and local-only alarms. Before removing signed-in alarm
      state from view, XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation and preserves truthful pending or
      failure status when cancellation cannot be confirmed. Signing in again

      existing history and does not by itself disable an installed browser
      extension's listeners or active-tab queries. You can clear the log at any
      time in the app (Automatic Activity Tracking → Reset tracked data).
      Removing only the app bundle may leave its container or Application Support
      data, so reset tracked data before removal if you want the locally stored
      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.
Where the data goes

While installed and enabled, the extension may query the active tab of the

      a periodic heartbeat. It sends that tab's web address and title locally to
      the XTimers Pro app on the same device. XTimers records and attributes that
      information only while website tracking is enabled and the supported
      browser is the frontmost Mac application.

While signed out, alarms are local-only and “This Device”
      is the only target. Signing in never moves one automatically. Use the

      “Failed,” “Sync Pending,” or another status.
      Rename or retire installations from the device controls when available.

Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed.       acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.

      the Mac to be awake, XTimers to be running, and required permissions to
      remain available. Offline devices can act later and may continue ringing
      until they receive and apply an update. Stop or snooze actions can take
      time to appear on another device. Do not treat XTimers as a guaranteed
      delivery service.

Sign Out of XTimers
Sign in with Apple, Google, an email code or a password. Some device settings and local-only data remain on their own device.

Signed-in users may synchronize timer and countdown names, task sets,
      timer state, session history, application settings, archived snapshots,
      reminders, and related metadata. If a user emails or publishes a report,
      XTimers processes the report content, title, recipient information, and
      delivery or link-expiration metadata needed to provide that feature.
      Published report links can be configured to expire after 1, 7, 30, 90, or
      365 days.

Signing out ends XTimers access on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation before hiding its signed-in alarm state;
      a pending or failed cancellation remains truthful when confirmation is
      unavailable. Signing out preserves local timers and other local data;
      XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset
      on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Removing or uninstalling the app can leave
      Application Support, container, or backup copies, depending on the
      platform and system settings. Signing out or uninstalling does not delete
      the Xin Account or server copies of connected XTimers data; use the
      authenticated account-deletion actions for that purpose.

Signing out ends XTimers sign-in on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. It does not delete the Xin Account, XTimers server data,
      or local timers and local-only alarms. Before removing signed-in alarm
      state from view, XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation and preserves truthful pending or
      failure status when cancellation cannot be confirmed. Signing in again
      can restore authorized synchronization.

The XTimers Pro app keeps the underlying activity log on your device. It
      is not continuously uploaded or synced
      to your other devices; only a user-requested report sends its displayed
      application names and derived hostnames. While tracking runs, raw events
      older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off in XTimers stops app
      recording and removes the app's native-host integration, but does not erase
      existing history and does not by itself disable an installed browser
      extension's listeners or active-tab queries. You can clear the log at any
      time in the app (Automatic Activity Tracking → Reset tracked data).
      Removing only the app bundle may leave its container or Application Support
      data, so reset tracked data before removal if you want the locally stored
      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

The extension inspects the web address and title of the active tab in the
      most recently focused supported browser. This extension-side query may
      occur even when another Mac app is currently frontmost. The extension does
      not read, store, or modify the content of a web page; does not inspect
      background tabs; does not keep a browsing history of its own; and does not
      request account identity, credentials, form data, or extension analytics.
      A web address or title can itself contain information chosen by the site
      or user. There are no ads and no third-party trackers in the extension.

The extension is not directed at children. Its active-tab behavior and

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.
Where the data goes

While installed and enabled, the extension may query the active tab of the

While signed out, alarms are local-only and “This Device”

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.

      a pending or failed cancellation remains truthful when confirmation is

      XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset

      application names and derived hostnames. While tracking runs, raw events
      older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off in XTimers stops app
      recording and removes the app's native-host integration, but does not erase
      existing history and does not by itself disable an installed browser
      extension's listeners or active-tab queries. You can clear the log at any
      time in the app (Automatic Activity Tracking → Reset tracked data).
      Removing only the app bundle may leave its container or Application Support
      data, so reset tracked data before removal if you want the locally stored
      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

      request account identity, credentials, form data, or extension analytics.
      A web address or title can itself contain information chosen by the site

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.

While installed and enabled, the extension may query the active tab of the

      information only while website tracking is enabled and the supported
      browser is the frontmost Mac application.

While signed out, alarms are local-only and “This Device”

      tracking, calendar features, synchronization, reports, custom sounds,

XTimers is operated by Xintech LLC. After a signed-in user gives explicit
      consent, XTimers may attempt to send a setup verification code to the
      user-entered proposed account phone number. After successful verification
      and opt-in, XTimers may attempt user-created timer/reminder SMS only to
      that same phone number and only when the user schedules them for
      themselves. XTimers does not send
      marketing SMS and does not allow users to send SMS to arbitrary
      third-party recipients. XTimers SMS is not a two-way chat or
      conversation service; inbound keywords are used only for STOP, HELP, START,
      and YES compliance handling.

XTimers may process a per-installation device identifier, push-notification
      token, platform, app version, build number, operating-system version,
      device model, service command or feature interaction, response status,
      response duration, and error information. These records are used to
      provide synchronization and notifications, operate the service, measure
      feature use, diagnose failures, improve performance, and prevent abuse.

XTimers product data, synchronization, reports, sounds, timers, alarms,
      and messaging remain XTimers services even though Xin Account provides
      sign-in. Features that work without sign-in may keep data on that
      installation. Signing in enables eligible product data to synchronize,
      but it never promotes a local-only alarm automatically; alarm promotion
      is an explicit user action.

XTimers provides separate controls for Xin Account identity, XTimers
      product data, synchronization, alarms, permissions, automatic activity
      tracking, calendar access, reports, diagnostics, and SMS. This page
      explains what each choice does.

      organization, request time, command name, and a stable hashed account

      existing history and does not by itself disable an installed browser

      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.

On iPhone and iPad, AlarmKit authorization and system scheduling are
      handled by Apple. On Mac, alarms require the Mac to be awake, XTimers to
      be running, and required permissions. Stop, snooze, fire, and cancellation
      actions can be synchronized so other installations can update their
      status, but an offline installation may act later or continue ringing.

On iPhone and iPad, system alarm delivery depends on AlarmKit
      authorization and operating-system scheduling. On Mac, delivery requires
      the Mac to be awake, XTimers to be running, and required permissions to
      remain available. Offline devices can act later and may continue ringing
      until they receive and apply an update. Stop or snooze actions can take
      time to appear on another device. Do not treat XTimers as a guaranteed
      delivery service.

Sign Out and Local Data
Sign Out of XTimers
Sign in with Apple, Google, an email code or a password. Some device settings and local-only data remain on their own device.

Signed-in users may synchronize timer and countdown names, task sets,
      timer state, session history, application settings, archived snapshots,
      reminders, and related metadata. If a user emails or publishes a report,
      XTimers processes the report content, title, recipient information, and
      delivery or link-expiration metadata needed to provide that feature.
      Published report links can be configured to expire after 1, 7, 30, 90, or
      365 days.

Signing out ends XTimers access on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation before hiding its signed-in alarm state;
      a pending or failed cancellation remains truthful when confirmation is
      unavailable. Signing out preserves local timers and other local data;
      XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset
      on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Removing or uninstalling the app can leave
      Application Support, container, or backup copies, depending on the
      platform and system settings. Signing out or uninstalling does not delete
      the Xin Account or server copies of connected XTimers data; use the
      authenticated account-deletion actions for that purpose.

Signing out ends XTimers sign-in on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. It does not delete the Xin Account, XTimers server data,
      or local timers and local-only alarms. Before removing signed-in alarm
      state from view, XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation and preserves truthful pending or
      failure status when cancellation cannot be confirmed. Signing in again
      can restore authorized synchronization.

The XTimers Pro app keeps the underlying activity log on your device. It
      is not continuously uploaded or synced
      to your other devices; only a user-requested report sends its displayed
      application names and derived hostnames. While tracking runs, raw events
      older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off in XTimers stops app
      recording and removes the app's native-host integration, but does not erase
      existing history and does not by itself disable an installed browser
      extension's listeners or active-tab queries. You can clear the log at any
      time in the app (Automatic Activity Tracking → Reset tracked data).
      Removing only the app bundle may leave its container or Application Support
      data, so reset tracked data before removal if you want the locally stored
      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

The core workspace includes timers, countdowns, clocks, task sets and reports. Mac adds menu-bar controls and World Calendar. iPhone supports Live Activities on compatible devices, while iPad makes room for larger task layouts.

The extension inspects the web address and title of the active tab in the
      most recently focused supported browser. This extension-side query may
      occur even when another Mac app is currently frontmost. The extension does
      not read, store, or modify the content of a web page; does not inspect
      background tabs; does not keep a browsing history of its own; and does not
      request account identity, credentials, form data, or extension analytics.
      A web address or title can itself contain information chosen by the site
      or user. There are no ads and no third-party trackers in the extension.

The extension is not directed at children. Its active-tab behavior and
      controls are the same for every user.

What is collected
What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.
Where the data goes

While installed and enabled, the extension may query the active tab of the
      most recently focused supported browser after tab or window events and on
      a periodic heartbeat. It sends that tab's web address and title locally to
      the XTimers Pro app on the same device. XTimers records and attributes that
      information only while website tracking is enabled and the supported
      browser is the frontmost Mac application.

While signed out, alarms are local-only and “This Device”

Signing out ends XTimers access on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation before hiding its signed-in alarm state;
      a pending or failed cancellation remains truthful when confirmation is
      unavailable. Signing out preserves local timers and other local data;
      XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset
      on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Removing or uninstalling the app can leave
      Application Support, container, or backup copies, depending on the
      platform and system settings. Signing out or uninstalling does not delete
      the Xin Account or server copies of connected XTimers data; use the
      authenticated account-deletion actions for that purpose.

Signing out ends XTimers sign-in on that device and pauses authenticated

      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

      request account identity, credentials, form data, or extension analytics.
      A web address or title can itself contain information chosen by the site

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.

XTimers currently sends email reports and user-created reminders only to
      the signed-in user's own verified XTimers account email address, and may
      attempt requested verification messages there. After a signed-in user
      gives explicit consent, XTimers may attempt to send a setup verification
      code to the user-entered proposed account phone number. User-created
      reminder SMS may be attempted only after successful verification and
      opt-in, and only to that same phone number. XTimers
      may process message content, delivery status,
      scheduled time, and provider response metadata to deliver and troubleshoot
      these messages.

XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset
      on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Signing out pauses authenticated synchronization
      and preserves local data. Removing or uninstalling the app may leave
      Application Support, container, or backup copies, depending on the
      platform and system settings. Use the authenticated Delete XTimers Data
      action for account-scoped deletion.

XTimers does not use the collected app data to track users across apps or
      websites owned by other companies for advertising. Xintech LLC does not
      sell SMS opt-in data or other app data. Xintech LLC does not share SMS
      opt-in data, phone numbers, or text-message consent with third parties or
      affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.

If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

Sign Out of XTimers
Sign in with Apple, Google, an email code or a password. Some device settings and local-only data remain on their own device.

Signed-in users may synchronize timer and countdown names, task sets,
      timer state, session history, application settings, archived snapshots,
      reminders, and related metadata. If a user emails or publishes a report,
      XTimers processes the report content, title, recipient information, and
      delivery or link-expiration metadata needed to provide that feature.
      Published report links can be configured to expire after 1, 7, 30, 90, or
      365 days.

Signing out ends XTimers access on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation before hiding its signed-in alarm state;
      a pending or failed cancellation remains truthful when confirmation is
      unavailable. Signing out preserves local timers and other local data;
      XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset
      on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Removing or uninstalling the app can leave
      Application Support, container, or backup copies, depending on the
      platform and system settings. Signing out or uninstalling does not delete
      the Xin Account or server copies of connected XTimers data; use the
      authenticated account-deletion actions for that purpose.

Signing out ends XTimers sign-in on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. It does not delete the Xin Account, XTimers server data,
      or local timers and local-only alarms. Before removing signed-in alarm
      state from view, XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation and preserves truthful pending or
      failure status when cancellation cannot be confirmed. Signing in again
      can restore authorized synchronization.

The XTimers Pro app keeps the underlying activity log on your device. It
      is not continuously uploaded or synced
      to your other devices; only a user-requested report sends its displayed
      application names and derived hostnames. While tracking runs, raw events
      older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off in XTimers stops app
      recording and removes the app's native-host integration, but does not erase
      existing history and does not by itself disable an installed browser
      extension's listeners or active-tab queries. You can clear the log at any
      time in the app (Automatic Activity Tracking → Reset tracked data).
      Removing only the app bundle may leave its container or Application Support
      data, so reset tracked data before removal if you want the locally stored
      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

The extension inspects the web address and title of the active tab in the
      most recently focused supported browser. This extension-side query may
      occur even when another Mac app is currently frontmost. The extension does
      not read, store, or modify the content of a web page; does not inspect
      background tabs; does not keep a browsing history of its own; and does not
      request account identity, credentials, form data, or extension analytics.
      A web address or title can itself contain information chosen by the site
      or user. There are no ads and no third-party trackers in the extension.

The extension is not directed at children. Its active-tab behavior and

Sign in with Apple, Google, an email code or a password. Some device settings and local-only data remain on their own device.

Signed-in users may synchronize timer and countdown names, task sets,

      reminders, and related metadata. If a user emails or publishes a report,
      XTimers processes the report content, title, recipient information, and
      delivery or link-expiration metadata needed to provide that feature.
      Published report links can be configured to expire after 1, 7, 30, 90, or
      365 days.

Signing out ends XTimers access on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation before hiding its signed-in alarm state;
      a pending or failed cancellation remains truthful when confirmation is
      unavailable. Signing out preserves local timers and other local data;
      XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset
      on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Removing or uninstalling the app can leave
      Application Support, container, or backup copies, depending on the
      platform and system settings. Signing out or uninstalling does not delete
      the Xin Account or server copies of connected XTimers data; use the
      authenticated account-deletion actions for that purpose.

Signing out ends XTimers sign-in on that device and pauses authenticated
      synchronization. It does not delete the Xin Account, XTimers server data,
      or local timers and local-only alarms. Before removing signed-in alarm
      state from view, XTimers makes a best-effort attempt to cancel system
      alarms owned by that installation and preserves truthful pending or
      failure status when cancellation cannot be confirmed. Signing in again
      can restore authorized synchronization.

The XTimers Pro app keeps the underlying activity log on your device. It
      is not continuously uploaded or synced
      to your other devices; only a user-requested report sends its displayed
      application names and derived hostnames. While tracking runs, raw events
      older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off in XTimers stops app
      recording and removes the app's native-host integration, but does not erase
      existing history and does not by itself disable an installed browser
      extension's listeners or active-tab queries. You can clear the log at any
      time in the app (Automatic Activity Tracking → Reset tracked data).
      Removing only the app bundle may leave its container or Application Support
      data, so reset tracked data before removal if you want the locally stored
      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

The extension inspects the web address and title of the active tab in the
      most recently focused supported browser. This extension-side query may
      occur even when another Mac app is currently frontmost. The extension does
      not read, store, or modify the content of a web page; does not inspect
      background tabs; does not keep a browsing history of its own; and does not
      request account identity, credentials, form data, or extension analytics.
      A web address or title can itself contain information chosen by the site
      or user. There are no ads and no third-party trackers in the extension.

The extension is not directed at children. Its active-tab behavior and

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.
Where the data goes

While installed and enabled, the extension may query the active tab of the
      most recently focused supported browser after tab or window events and on
      a periodic heartbeat. It sends that tab's web address and title locally to
      the XTimers Pro app on the same device. XTimers records and attributes that
      information only while website tracking is enabled and the supported
      browser is the frontmost Mac application.

While signed out, alarms are local-only and “This Device”
      is the only target. Signing in never moves one automatically. Use the
      app's explicit promotion action if you want an eligible local alarm to
      become shared. For a shared alarm, use each device's “Rings On” switch to

      “Failed,” “Sync Pending,” or another status.
      Rename or retire installations from the device controls when available.
      Deleting a local-only alarm removes it only from that installation.

What the extension does

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a
      separate XTimers account identifier, its Xin Account association, product
      settings, and the contact email used for requested XTimers messages. When
      the user sets up SMS features, XTimers also processes the proposed account
      phone number, its verification status, and SMS consent records. XTimers uses this product information to
      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.
Where the data goes

While installed and enabled, the extension may query the active tab of the
      most recently focused supported browser after tab or window events and on
      a periodic heartbeat. It sends that tab's web address and title locally to
      the XTimers Pro app on the same device. XTimers records and attributes that
      information only while website tracking is enabled and the supported
      browser is the frontmost Mac application.

While signed out, alarms are local-only and “This Device”
      is the only target. Signing in never moves one automatically. Use the
      app's explicit promotion action if you want an eligible local alarm to
      become shared. For a shared alarm, use each device's “Rings On” switch to

      “Failed,” “Sync Pending,” or another status.
      Rename or retire installations from the device controls when available.
      Deleting a local-only alarm removes it only from that installation.

      a pending or failed cancellation remains truthful when confirmation is
      unavailable. Signing out preserves local timers and other local data;
      XTimers does not currently provide a separate whole-app local-data reset
      on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Removing or uninstalling the app can leave
      Application Support, container, or backup copies, depending on the
      platform and system settings. Signing out or uninstalling does not delete
      the Xin Account or server copies of connected XTimers data; use the
      authenticated account-deletion actions for that purpose.

      existing history and does not by itself disable an installed browser
      extension's listeners or active-tab queries. You can clear the log at any
      time in the app (Automatic Activity Tracking → Reset tracked data).
      Removing only the app bundle may leave its container or Application Support
      data, so reset tracked data before removal if you want the locally stored
      activity erased.

The active-tab report is delivered only to the XTimers Pro app running on your own computer — either through the app's local native-messaging host or a loopback (%1$@) connection to the app on the same machine. The extension itself has no remote host and does not transmit the active-tab report over the internet. If the user later asks XTimers Pro to email or publish an activity report, the selected report's application names and derived website hostnames may be sent to XTimers' service for that requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included, as explained in the %2$@main Privacy Policy%3$@.

When a user connects XTimers to a Xin Account, XTimers processes a

      synchronize XTimers data, deliver requested messages, prevent abuse, and
      provide XTimers product support.

When a user opens an external benefit or support link, XTimers does not
      append an account identifier or personal data to the outbound link. The
      destination still receives ordinary browser and network information, such
      as an IP address and user agent, under its own privacy practices.

When creating an online report link, choose an expiration of 1, 7, 30,
      90, or 365 days. The link stops working after that expiration. To avoid
      uploading report content, use local copy or export options instead of
      email or online publishing.

When the user enables automatic activity tracking, XTimers records application activity on the user's Mac. Active browser-tab web-address and title tracking is available only in the separately distributed XTimers Pro edition (downloaded from xintechllc.com, not the App Store); it never applies to the App Store edition. The underlying activity log is maintained on the device and is not continuously uploaded. While tracking runs, raw events older than 365 days are removed. Turning tracking off stops XTimers app recording and its browser integration but does not erase existing history; Reset tracked data clears that local history. An installed browser extension can continue its own active-tab queries and local delivery attempts until the user disables or removes it. XTimers Pro stores the full active-tab web address and title locally, while activity summaries derive the website hostname. If the user explicitly emails or publishes an activity report, the selected report content, including application names and derived hostnames shown in that report, is sent to XTimers' service to perform the requested action; raw web addresses and titles are not included in those reports. The separately distributed browser component is covered by the %1$@XTimers Activity Extension Privacy Policy%2$@.

When the user turns on the Personal Calendar Overlay and grants permission,
      XTimers reads events from the calendars the user selects in Apple Calendar,
      including any iCloud, Google, Outlook, or subscribed calendars already
      configured there. XTimers does not connect to those calendar providers
      directly and never requests their account credentials; Apple Calendar
      continues to synchronize them under the user's own settings.
      Event details—including title, start and end time, all-day and cancellation
      state, and calendar name, identifier, and color—are read on the device to
      display events or trigger user-selected advance alerts and are not
      uploaded to XTimers' service. On Mac, XTimers may locally examine an event
      web address, location, or notes to identify a supported HTTPS conference
      link and open it when the user chooses. XTimers stores on the installation the
      feature choices, selected-calendar identifiers, alert lead time, short-lived
      alert acknowledgements, and a record of which privacy explanation was
      acknowledged. XTimers never creates, edits, or deletes calendar events.
